podcast.title: Keeping Ska Alive
podcast.body: The Toasters, along with The Uptones, played a role in maintaining the Ska scene after the second wave had largely diminished, ensuring the genre didn't completely die out. "Groups like The Toasters and The Uptones kept things alive while SCAT receded into the background."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Toasters – Founded by British Expat Rob Hingley in New York; Most Important American Ska Band of the 1980s; Founded Moon Ska Records
podcast.body: The Toasters were the most important American ska band of the 1980s. Founder Rob Hingley was a Brit who moved to New York only to find almost no one knew about the British ska scene, so he formed a band based on Two-Tone traditions. Beyond touring and recording, Hingley also established Moon Ska Records, which eventually became the largest and most important independent ska label in America, distributing dozens of bands across the continent. Moon Ska Records had a business until 2000, though some European operations survived. "Out of all the Skah bands of the early and middle 80s, no American group did more to popularize this sound in the US than the Toasters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: A Not-So Brief History of Ska: Part 2

xref.title: Planet Smashers (Montreal, 1994) – Founded Stomp Records; Survived the "Ska Death" of 1999–2002
xref.body: The Planet Smashers formed in 1994 and created their own label, Stomp Records, which has promoted dozens of ska, ska-punk, and ska-friendly bands including Buckle 9, Bedouin Soundclash, The Flatliners, The New York Ska-Jazz Ensemble, St. Alvia, and even The Toasters. The ska scene largely crashed in the US between 1999 and 2002, described by Matt Collier as "brutal" — the band stopped touring in the US for three years. The recovery beginning in 2003 brought ska back to its natural home as a subculture. "You do not want to be Scott from 1999 to 2002. You just didn't do it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
